answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independently checked work is fraudulent. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up real capital, and successful cheating risks losing it; fake names alone do not multiply influence. A knoll-side verifier might tag a suspicious umber-colored batch, while a ripple of matching claims triggers extra review, making large-scale Sybil attempts costly without treating identity counts as proof.
